analyst_view.overall: League leaders Dortmund (24 points, unbeaten in 12 league games, seven conceded in ten, six clean sheets) host fifth-placed Leverkusen (19 points, two wins in a row) on Sunday evening; Leverkusen won the last meeting here 1-0 in April, Dortmund's last home league defeat. Serhou Guirassy is back after coming off the bench in Tuesday's 1-1 at Arsenal, and Dortmund have four days' rest; Emre Can, Konstantelias, Lerma and Inácio are out, as the numbers assume. Leverkusen won 2-0 at Dinamo Zagreb on Thursday, taking off Schick and Maza around the hour to save legs, so they have three days and a flight before Sunday; Terrier and Eichhorn are out (counted), while Guela Doué is back from injury. Daniel Schlager referees (counted). News was from two outlets only, so the view leans mainly on the short turnaround and Dortmund's tight defence.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 1.9 for Dortmund. Dortmund under Kovac play tight games (seven conceded in ten, most wins by one goal), and Leverkusen arrive three days after a Europa League trip to Zagreb, which the numbers do not see, even if Schick and Maza were rested early. Guirassy's return helps Dortmund, but he is only just fit, so I lean a little lower, to about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners and already add for Leverkusen's 41 corners in their last six. Doué's return at full-back adds width, but Dortmund's game is built on control rather than crossing, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, already adding 12% for Leverkusen's 16 cards in six, trimming Dortmund for only six, and adding 8% for Schlager (4.2 a game). A top game between two possession sides is not a grudge match, so I stay at 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.4 shots, already lifted for Dortmund's 92 in six and Leverkusen's recent volume. Leverkusen's tired legs after Zagreb could cost a few shots, but Dortmund at home with Guirassy back may take a few more, so these roughly cancel and I stay at 27.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target, 5.3 for Dortmund. Dortmund allow few clear chances (25 on target conceded in six), Leverkusen's sharpness after a Thursday away game in Europe is a fair doubt, and Terrier is still out, so I take a little off, to about 9.0.
